cards.back: To participate or become involved in an activity. "Students should engage actively in classroom discussions." Common collocations: engage in, engage with, actively engage.
The same in amount, number, or size. "All citizens have equal rights under the law." Common collocations: equal opportunity, equal rights, equal access.
A mistake or something incorrect. "The report contained several factual errors." Common collocations: common error, human error, margin of error.
Relating to a group of people with shared culture or nationality. "The city has a diverse ethnic population." Common collocations: ethnic group, ethnic minority, ethnic diversity.
Something that happens, especially something important. "The concert was a major cultural event." Common collocations: special event, major event, sporting event.
To develop gradually over time. "Language continues to evolve with each generation." Common collocations: gradually evolve, evolve over time, constantly evolve.
To deliberately not include something or someone. "The price excludes delivery charges." Common collocations: exclude from, deliberately exclude, exclude the possibility.
To reveal or make visible something hidden. "The investigation exposed serious problems in the system." Common collocations: expose to, expose the truth, expose weaknesses.
The degree or size of something. "The extent of the damage was not immediately clear." Common collocations: to some extent, full extent, great extent.
Coming from or relating to the outside. "The building has excellent external insulation." Common collocations: external factors, external pressure, external appearance.
Very great in degree or intensity. "The region experiences extreme temperatures in summer." Common collocations: extreme weather, extreme conditions, extreme measures.
A building or place that provides a particular service. "The university has excellent sports facilities." Common collocations: research facility, medical facility, training facility.
Relating to money or finance. "The company faced serious financial difficulties." Common collocations: financial support, financial crisis, financial system.
Able to change or adapt easily. "Modern workers need flexible skills." Common collocations: flexible approach, flexible working, remain flexible.
Following official or traditional rules and customs. "A formal letter requires specific formatting." Common collocations: formal education, formal agreement, formal occasion.
Belonging to an earlier time; previous. "The former president gave a speech yesterday." Common collocations: former student, former employee, former partner.
The basis or underlying principle of something. "Trust is the foundation of any good relationship." Common collocations: strong foundation, lay the foundation, solid foundation.
A structure that gives shape or support. "The picture looks better in a wooden frame." Common collocations: time frame, frame of reference, metal frame.
Happening often or regularly. "She makes frequent visits to her elderly parents." Common collocations: frequent traveler, frequent occurrence, most frequent.
The purpose or role of something. "The main function of the heart is to pump blood." Common collocations: basic function, main function, function properly.
Money saved or made available for a particular purpose. "The school needs funds for new equipment." Common collocations: raise funds, emergency fund, pension fund.
An aim or desired result. "Her goal is to complete her degree in three years." Common collocations: achieve a goal, set a goal, long-term goal.
A level or mark indicating quality or performance. "She received the highest grade in her class." Common collocations: good grade, grade level, passing grade.
An amount of money given officially for a particular purpose. "The research team received a government grant." Common collocations: research grant, grant funding, apply for a grant.
A formal promise that something will happen or is true. "The company offers a money-back guarantee." Common collocations: guarantee quality, no guarantee, lifetime guarantee.
To show or direct someone in the right direction. "The teacher will guide students through the assignment." Common collocations: guide through, user guide, tour guide.
To emphasize or draw attention to something important. "The report highlights several key findings." Common collocations: highlight the importance, highlight the problem, main highlight.
To deliberately pay no attention to something. "You should not ignore warning signs." Common collocations: ignore advice, choose to ignore, completely ignore.
To explain or make clear using examples or pictures. "This chart illustrates the main trends." Common collocations: clearly illustrate, illustrate the point, illustrate with examples.
A picture or visual representation of something. "The satellite captured a detailed image of the city." Common collocations: public image, mental image, brand image.
A person who comes to live permanently in a foreign country. "Many immigrants have contributed to the nation's economy." Common collocations: illegal immigrant, immigrant community, immigrant worker.
To show or point out something. "Recent studies indicate a growing trend." Common collocations: clearly indicate, indicate that, strongly indicate.
Happening at the beginning; first. "The initial response was very positive." Common collocations: initial stage, initial reaction, initial investment.
To cause physical harm or damage to someone. "Three people were injured in the accident." Common collocations: seriously injure, injure yourself, badly injured.
Information, ideas, or effort put into something. "We welcome your input on this project." Common collocations: valuable input, user input, provide input.
An example or single occurrence of something. "This is just one instance of the problem." Common collocations: for instance, rare instance, specific instance.

An organization established for a specific purpose, especially education or research. "She works at a medical research institute." Common collocations: research institute, educational institute, training institute.
To teach or give orders to someone. "The manual instructs users on proper installation." Common collocations: instruct students, clearly instruct, instruct to do.
Having or showing the ability to learn and understand quickly. "She is a highly intelligent student." Common collocations: highly intelligent, intelligent design, intelligent behavior.
To communicate or work together with others. "Children learn by interacting with their environment." Common collocations: interact with, directly interact, interact socially.
Existing or happening inside something. "The company conducted an internal investigation." Common collocations: internal affairs, internal conflict, internal structure.
To explain the meaning of something. "Different people may interpret the data differently." Common collocations: interpret as, interpret the results, correctly interpret.
To examine or study something carefully to discover facts. "Police are investigating the incident." Common collocations: investigate thoroughly, investigate whether, investigate the cause.
To put money, effort, or time into something to make a profit or achieve a result. "The government plans to invest in renewable energy." Common collocations: invest in, invest heavily, invest time.
A newspaper or magazine dealing with a particular subject. "The research was published in a scientific journal." Common collocations: academic journal, medical journal, keep a journal.
To show or prove that something is right or reasonable. "How can you justify such high prices?" Common collocations: justify the decision, difficult to justify, fully justify.
A piece of paper or material attached to something giving information about it. "Read the label carefully before use." Common collocations: warning label, product label, attach a label.
Work, especially physical work. "The project required months of hard labour." Common collocations: manual labour, labour force, labour market.
A thickness of material covering a surface. "The cake has three layers of chocolate." Common collocations: top layer, protective layer, multiple layers.
An educational talk given to a group of people. "The professor gave an interesting lecture on climate change." Common collocations: attend a lecture, give a lecture, lecture hall.
